title: Ancient Trees in Vietnam: Places to Explore
meta_description: The last of Vietnam's first heritage trees, a newspaper's banyan in Hanoi and Hoi An's bugle band tree. {trees} trees across {places} places in Vietnam.
intro: Vietnam's heritage tree title was first given in 2010, to nine wild mangoes at a Hanoi temple, and within a few years eight of them were dead. The survivor at Voi Phuc Temple is one of the trees we map in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Hoi An. Most of the others are banyans their cities have built a life around. In Hanoi a newspaper has worked in the courtyard of one since 1954. In Saigon a five-trunked banyan stands on a block the French once handed to Spain for a consulate. Hoi An names one after a French-era military bugle band that practised in its shade, and another is slowly swallowing the brick shrine set into its trunk. On the island of Cu Lao Cham, two trees of different species have knotted their crowns into one roof over a temple yard. Only one tree here has a planting date, a bodhi at Tran Quoc Pagoda, set in 1959 by India's president as a return gift for a tree Ho Chi Minh had given India. The other ages are press figures and local accounts of several hundred years, and we give them as that.
